title: Type scales and spacing scales — Image Wiki

rules.rule: If two adjacent text sizes differ by less than 15%, they are competing rather than ranking and should be removed.
rules.evidence: Sort them. Any two within about 15% of each other are competing, not ranking.

rules.rule: If a spacing scale contains gaps that play the same role but have different values, it indicates arbitrary choices rather than a deliberate system.
rules.evidence: Look at the two gaps between list rows: 9 px and 11 px. They play the same role, so they should be the same number, and nobody decided that they should not be.

rules.rule: If a type scale is defined as fixed pixel values, it may fail on small screens where steps collapse into one value or consume too much screen real estate.
rules.evidence: The honest detail is the middle. On small screens points 27 and 24 both render at 21 px — two steps collapse into one value.
